evidence: judge-context/checks.json:2 reports patch_applies=true, and the generated tree differs from base only in the four files named in patch.diff (pytorch.json, tensorflow.json, image_uris.py, test_retrieve.py).

Executed reference tests/unit/sagemaker/image_uris/test_graviton.py::test_graviton_tensorflow and ::test_graviton_pytorch against a scratch copy of generated/ (originals untouched): both FAILED with ValueError 'Unsupported image scope: None'. Traceback: generated/src/sagemaker/image_uris.py:154 -> _config_for_framework_and_scope -> _validate_arg at :293. The reference test calls image_uris.retrieve(framework, region, instance_type=..., version=...) with no image_scope (reference/tests/unit/sagemaker/image_uris/test_graviton.py:61).

PASS_TO_PASS: executed tests/unit/sagemaker/image_uris (excluding jumpstart, which needs a real mock package) plus tests/unit/test_pytorch.py on generated/: 1675 passed, with a shim for the missing 'mock' module. The base tree gave 1630 passed under the same shim, so the 45-test count gap is only partly explained (the candidate's 9 new test cases account for 9 of it; the remaining 36 were not traced). Both trees had zero failures. The candidate's own tests/unit/sagemaker/image_uris/test_retrieve.py: 33 passed with the shim. The checks.json collection error (test_retrieve.py:19, 'No module named mock') comes from the import already present in base test_retrieve.py:19, so it is environmental, not caused by the patch.

criteria.deficiency: Both FAIL_TO_PASS tests from the reference fail on the candidate. The candidate only resolves Graviton images when the caller passes image_scope='inference' explicitly, so the reference's default-path behavior is not met.

evidence: Image config data is placed in src/sagemaker/image_uri_config/pytorch.json (generated: :52-56 'graviton' processor in the inference scope, :656-700 1.12.1 entry with nested 'graviton' object) and tensorflow.json (generated: :266, :1473-1510). This matches the reference's JSON-config location.

Selection logic is placed in src/sagemaker/image_uris.py: family detection at generated :362-363 (_is_graviton_family), processor selection at :402-403 (_processor), and graviton repo/tag handling at :185-199 (retrieve). These are the same modules the reference changes.

Reference contract: retrieve() with a Graviton instance type and no image_scope resolves to the '*-inference-graviton' repo. The reference does this with _get_image_scope_for_instance_type called before config load (reference/src/sagemaker/image_uris.py:155, per reference.diff hunk '@@ -151,6 +152,7 @@'), and the reference test relies on it (reference/tests/unit/sagemaker/image_uris/test_graviton.py:61).

Candidate contract: retrieve() only reaches the graviton branch after the scope is already resolved. generated/src/sagemaker/image_uris.py:154 passes the caller's image_scope (None) to _config_for_framework_and_scope, which raises at :293 (see the executed run in patch_and_checks). So a Graviton request without image_scope raises instead of returning an image URI.
Candidate's own test (generated/tests/unit/sagemaker/image_uris/test_retrieve.py:438-470) always passes image_scope='inference', which hides this contract gap.
criteria.deficiency: Public retrieve() contract is not met for the default-scope call with a Graviton instance type. It raises ValueError where the reference returns the graviton image URI.

evidence: The patch adds no imports. The image_uris.py import block (generated lines 14-30) is unchanged from base image_uris.py:14-27, and the patch hunks for image_uris.py start at line 182, after the imports.
The 're' module used by _is_graviton_family was already imported (base image_uris.py:19).

Graviton is registered through the existing config schema: 'graviton' is added to the inference scope's processors list (generated pytorch.json:52-56, tensorflow.json:266), and per-version graviton data is added to the versions (generated pytorch.json:656-700, tensorflow.json:1473-1510).

_processor consumes that registry through available_processors (generated image_uris.py:402-403), so the registration is actually used. This is a valid alternative to the reference's separate 'inference_graviton' scope; the missing scope-resolution behavior is captured under api_contract and requirement_intent.
The patch touches only JSON config, image_uris.py, and tests. It adds no packages or requirements (patch.diff file list).

Graviton logic sits in the same layers the reference uses: config data in image_uri_config JSON, URI assembly in image_uris.py, and processor selection next to the existing family logic in _processor (generated image_uris.py:402-403).
The placement problem (scope resolution happens before instance-type processing) is a behavior and extension-point issue, recorded under extension_point_adherence.

The existing extension point for instance-type-driven config selection runs before config load: base src/sagemaker/image_uris.py:149-153 derives _framework from the instance type (_get_inference_tool) and then calls _config_for_framework_and_scope(_framework, image_scope, ...) at :154.
The reference follows that pattern, adding _get_image_scope_for_instance_type before config load (reference/src/sagemaker/image_uris.py:155).

The candidate instead handles graviton after config load and scope validation: generated image_uris.py:185-199 (if processor == 'graviton') and :402-403 (_processor). Instance type never influences scope selection, so a parallel path is created that works only when image_scope is passed explicitly.
criteria.deficiency: The candidate does not use the existing instance-type-to-config selection step (base image_uris.py:149-154). Graviton selection is bolted on after scope validation, so the graviton config is unreachable unless the caller passes image_scope='inference'.

evidence: The change stays within URI resolution and static config data. There is no transport, persistence, or framework-layer coupling.
The helper _is_graviton_family (generated image_uris.py:362-363) is private and stays in the module that owns the family parsing (_processor, base image_uris.py:348-396).

Repo convention: container_version is keyed by processor (base image_uris.py:182-183 'version_config["container_version"][processor]'). The reference follows it with container_version: {"cpu": "ubuntu20.04"} (reference pytorch.json/tensorflow.json graviton entries).

The candidate adds a new nested 'graviton' object with a plain string container_version (generated pytorch.json:689-694, tensorflow.json:1503-1508), and reads it as a string (generated image_uris.py:190). This bypasses the processor-keyed container_version shape and adds a new config shape that nothing else uses.

The family check uses an open regex (generated image_uris.py:362-363) instead of an explicit allowlist, which the reference expresses as module constants (reference/src/sagemaker/fw_utils.py, GRAVITON_ALLOWED_TARGET_INSTANCE_FAMILY). This is a style and maintainability divergence from the repo's explicit-constant pattern.
criteria.deficiency: The new graviton config shape (plain-string container_version nested under a version) departs from the processor-keyed container_version convention used throughout the image config files and in image_uris.py:182-183.

evidence: Intent: Graviton instance types (ml.c6g/t4g/r6g/m6g per reference fw_utils.py) on TensorFlow and PyTorch should resolve to the '*-inference-graviton' DLC image in every region without the caller specifying a scope (reference/tests/unit/sagemaker/image_uris/test_graviton.py:61). Executed on candidate: both cases raise ValueError 'Unsupported image scope: None'.
Candidate's behavior works only when image_scope='inference' is passed (test_retrieve.py:438-470). It also has no graviton image for training, which matches the reference.

Scope creep versus the reference allowlist: generated image_uris.py:362-363 uses a regex that also matches g-prefixed families. I ran _is_graviton_family('g5g') -> True. Before the patch, g-prefixed families went to the GPU image (base image_uris.py:385-386), so if a g5g-style name reaches this path it now selects a CPU Graviton image. I did not verify that such an instance type exists in the SageMaker catalog.
criteria.deficiency: Core intent is not met: a Graviton instance request without an explicit image_scope fails for both frameworks, which is what the reference test checks. The family matching is also broader than the reference allowlist, so it can map non-Graviton-CPU families to the Graviton CPU image.
